rm-recursive-force.forbids: rm with both a recursive and a force flag
rm-recursive-force.instead: remove a file with rm -i /full/path/to/file; remove a directory by its literal path without -f

rm-protected.forbids: a recursive rm of the root, a home, a shared tree or a system directory
rm-protected.instead: name the one file or directory you mean by its full path

empty-variable.forbids: a destructive command (rm, mv, cp -r, chmod -R, chown -R, find -delete, truncate, shred, dd of=) whose path holds a variable or substitution, which may be empty or unexpanded
empty-variable.instead: expand the value yourself and write the full path, or write the variable as ${NAME:?} so that an empty value stops the command

find-root.instead: find . -name PATTERN, or find in the one directory you mean

kill-by-pattern.forbids: pkill and killall, which match processes of every user of the account by name or pattern
kill-by-pattern.instead: kill PID of your own process

other-worktree.forbids: a git command that changes state in a work directory of another agent or in a shared checkout
other-worktree.instead: change your own work directory, and ask the owner of another one

no-verify.forbids: git with --no-verify, which skips the hooks of the repository
no-verify.instead: fix what the hook refused and commit again

git-push.forbids: git push by an agent or to a remote that the policy does not name
git-push.instead: leave pushing to the agent the policy names

pipe-to-shell.forbids: downloading with curl or wget and piping it into a shell
pipe-to-shell.instead: download to a file, read it, then run it on purpose

sudo.forbids: sudo by an agent the policy does not name
sudo.instead: ask the person who administers the host
